data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement rails-sdk-add phase: when --template=rails and not --no-sdk, append `gem \"strata\", github: \"navapbc/strata-sdk-rails\"` (gem name is `strata`, not `strata-sdk-rails`, per spike) to the generated Gemfile. Idempotent grep-before-append. No Ruby/bundler on host; user's first `make build` runs `bundle install` inside Docker.
**Why**: Strata SDK provides the Rails-first integration that motivates this rewrite; gem-add is a single-line append, but must be idempotent to allow safe re-runs.
**Scope**:
- IN: grep for existing `gem \"strata\"` line; append only if missing; --no-sdk skips the phase; --template=nextjs and --template=flask never invoke the phase.
- OUT: Bundling/installing gems on host; gem version pinning logic; upstream contribution to template-application-rails (filed as separate non-blocking ticket).

## Done Definitions
- When complete, --template=rails (default) appends the gem line exactly once even on multiple runs ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, --no-sdk skips the append; gem line is absent ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, --template=nextjs and --template=flask never trigger the phase ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, post-build SDK functional check (`make rails-runner CMD='require \"strata\"; puts Strata::VERSION'`) returns a non-empty version string ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for idempotency, --no-sdk skip, template variant skips

## Considerations
- [Reliability] Idempotency strict — grep-before-append must not match within comments or other gems
- [Testing] SDK functional check requires Docker; gate the test on Docker availability

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a Rails-template user, the strata-sdk-rails gem is appended to Gemfile idempotently
